I fixed the crash in `app/src/main/kotlin/vn/shelftap/lab/MainActivity.kt`. I couldn't build or run the app here, so this is checked by reading the code only.

**Cause:** The "Load catalog" click handler called `CatalogClient().fetchCatalog()` directly on the UI thread. That method uses OkHttp's blocking `execute()`, and Android throws `NetworkOnMainThreadException` for network work on the main thread.

**Change:**
- The click handler now sets "Loading...", then runs the fetch on a background `Thread`.
- The result is written to the TextView via `runOnUiThread`, since views may only be updated on the main thread.
- The catch block now catches `Exception` instead of `IOException`. `fetchCatalog()` uses `check(...)` for non-2xx responses, which throws `IllegalStateException`, and that would have crashed the app even after the threading fix.

I didn't touch `CatalogClient.kt` or the session-token handling, since neither is involved in this crash. A plain `Thread` avoids adding a coroutines dependency; if the project already uses coroutines, moving this into `lifecycleScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO)` would be the more idiomatic version.
